Mina — logging the answers below and attaching a sample CSV (deletion-log-sample.csv). See the CSV and the inline notes.

Summary (short):
- Proofchain design: we maintain an append-only audit log per region. Each audit entry stores a record payload and a SHA256 over (prev_entry_hash || payload). The entry also records the operation id (op_id), UTC timestamp, actor_id, object_hash (SHA256 of object identifier + metadata), and region. This produces a tamper-evident linked list (proofchain) per partition.
- Sample export: deletion-log-sample.csv contains 50 sanitized rows. Each row has: op_id,timestamp_utc,actor_id,object_hash,prev_hash,region,lifecycle_state.
- Backups/snapshots: For EU tenants we retain daily snapshots for 30 days and backups for 90 days in archive tier unless customer contract specifies a shorter window. Snapshot manifests reference object ids and are included in the audit export when relevant.
- Backup purge path: archive tier deletions trigger a purge job which records its operation in the proofchain; the purge record references the deletion op_id(s) it reconciled.
- Key caveat: forensic snapshots taken outside of standard backup windows (ad-hoc exports) are handled by the customer's export governance; we mark those exports in the audit log.

Files attached: deletion-log-sample.csv (sanitized), proof-instructions.txt (small script + verification steps).

If you want, we can include the verification script as a short notebook, but CSV + plain script is usually fine for auditors.

—Vivek

Kirk / Amira,

Per your request, attached is a compact evidence packet for tenant T-5472. The package is intentionally sanitized to remove customer PII while preserving proofchain integrity. Contents: 
- proofchain-overview.pdf (one page) — explains our SHA256 append-only audit approach and where logs are stored (immutable archive + signed manifests).
- deletion-log-sample.csv (50 anonymized rows) — columns: op_id,timestamp_utc,actor_id,object_hash,prev_hash,region,lifecycle_state. CSV includes three representative deletion flows: immediate object deletion, archival purge, and scheduled TTL expiry.
- proof-instructions.txt — a short script and steps auditors can run locally to recompute hashes and verify the chain for the sample rows.

Direct answers to your original bullets:
1) Sample of deletion events: included (deletion-log-sample.csv). Rows have been redacted to eliminate tenant-specific names; object_hash values remain intact so auditors can validate the chain.
2) Proofchain explanation: see proofchain-overview.pdf. In short: each audit entry records prev_hash and payload; auditors recompute payload hashes and then verify the linked sequence via SHA256(prev_hash || payload). We also record a signed daily manifest (kept in immutable storage) that contains a root hash of the day's append-only log.
3) TTL / backup retention: FinLedger's contract uses standard EU profile: daily snapshots retained 30 days; backups archived 90 days. After the archive retention expires we run a purge workflow and record the purge op_id in the proofchain.

Related artifacts & links:
- Drive folder with packet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB3-proofchain-samples
- HubSpot ticket: HS-78901 — auditors are linked to the ticket for traceability.

Attachments are CSV/PDF/TXT as noted. If you need a notarized timestamp or a vendor-signed attestation for the root hash we can route to Legal and schedule.

Let me know if you want the notebook verification instead of the plain script or if the auditors want JSON-formatted exports.

Regards,
